text.p: Performance Nutrition Inc shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against the company alleging misrepresentation of material information about the company's business outlook, the plaintiff lawyers said.
Weiss & Yourman said in a statement a class action lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas on behalf of the shareholders.

The complaint charged the company, former President, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Gary Lewellyn and former Secretary and Treasurer Tamara Halling with violations of the 1934 Securities Exchange Act, the lawyers said.

Weiss & Yourman said the complaint charged the company with misrepresenting or omitting material information during the class period concerning the company's business, outlook, suspension and embezzlement conviction of Lewellyn.

The lawyers also said the complaint charged misrepresentation of material information about the absence of clinical support that the company's KidsPLEX product could be used in the treatment of Attention Deficit Disorder.

The complaint also alleged that the company employed improper accounting practices, that its earnings for the nine months ending June 30 were misstated and that its stock price was thereby artificially inflated, the lawyers said.
The company was not immediately available to comment on the suit.
The plaintiff sought to recover damages on behalf of class members.
